nodes.name: Lemma 2.1
nodes.statement: For any $S^{+}, S^{-}\subset \mathbb{R}^{k}$ and projection $\pi$ onto a subspace indexed by coordinates $\Sigma \subset \lbrace 1, \dots , k\rbrace$, if $\pi(S^{+})$ and $\pi (S^{-})$ are linearly separable with margin $\mu$, then $S^{+}$ and $S^-$ are also linearly separable with margin at least $\mu$.

nodes.name: Theorem 1.3, Theorem 1.4: aligned for finite sets $X^+, X^-$ aligned
nodes.statement:
Fix any $\eta \in (0, 1)$ and $\delta$-separated $X^{+}, X^{-}\subset R\mathbb{B}_{2}^{d}$ with $d\geq 2$.
itemize
	\item If $X^+$ and $X^-$ are finite, let $N:=\vert X^{+}\vert +\vert X^{-}\vert$, and let $\gamma: =\delta^{2}/8Rd$.
	\item Otherwise, let $N$ be the $(\delta, 64\delta^{-2}R^{3}d)$-mutual complexity of $X^+$ and $X^-$, and let $\gamma:= \delta^2/16Rd$.
itemize
For a one-layer RINN $\Phi(x):=\relax(Wx+b)$ with weights $W\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times d}$ and bias $b\sim \mathrm{Unif}\left([-\lambda, \lambda]^n\right)$, the sets $\Phi(X^{+}), \Phi (X^{-})\subset\mathbb{R}^{n}$ are linearly separable with probability at least $1-\eta$ by a margin at least $\mathcal{M}(\gamma,N)$ if width $n$ and maximal bias $\lambda$ satisfy either of the following, depending on how weights $W$ is sampled:
enumerate
\item[(i)] $n\geq \frac{\log (N/\eta)}{p}$ and $\lambda\geq R$ if each row of the weight matrix $W_i\stackrel{iid}{\sim} \mathrm{Unif}(\mathbb{S}^{d-1})$,
\item[(ii)] $n\geq \frac{10\log (N/\eta)}{p}$ and $\lambda\geq 3R\sqrt{d}$ if weights $W\sim \relax(0, I_{n\times d})$ are Gaussian,
enumerate
where we recall that $\relax(0, I_{n\times d})$ means each entry is i.i.d. $\relax(0, 1)$, and define
equation
p:=\frac{R}{8(d-1)\lambda}\left(\frac{\delta^{2}}{8R^{2}}\right)^{d}\quad\text{and}\quad\mathcal{M}(\gamma,N):=\sqrt{\frac{4R(R+\gamma)}{N(1+2R/\gamma)^{2N}-N}}.
equation

There exists a constant $C = C(\delta, R)>0$ such that the following holds. Fix any $\eta \in (0, 1)$ and $\delta$-separated $X^{+}, X^{-}\subset R\mathbb{B}_{2}^{d}$ with $d\geq 2$.


itemize
	\item If $X^+$ and $X^-$ are finite, let $N:=\vert X^{+}\vert +\vert X^{-}\vert$, and let $\gamma: =\delta^{2}/18R\sqrt{k}$.
	\item Otherwise, let $N$ be the $(\delta, 144\delta^{-2}R^{3}\sqrt{k})$-mutual complexity of $X^+$ and $X^-$, and let $\gamma:= \delta^{2}/36R\sqrt{k}$, where in both cases we let
equation
 k := C\left(\frac{32R}{\delta^2}\right)^2\left(w\left((X^+-X^-)\cup X^+\cup X^-\right)^2+R^2\right).
equation
itemize
For a one-layer RINN $\Phi(x):=\relax(Wx+b)$ with standard Gaussian weights $W\sim \relax(0, I_{n\times d})$ and bias $b\sim \mathrm{Unif}\left([-\lambda, \lambda]^n\right)$, the sets $\Phi(X^{+}), \Phi (X^{-})\subset\mathbb{R}^{n}$ are linearly separable with probability at least $1-\eta$ by a margin at least $\mathcal{M}(\gamma,N)$ defined in (1.1), provided maximal bias $\lambda \geq 9R\sqrt{k}/8$ and width equation
n \geq \frac{\log (N/\eta)}{q}, \quad \text{where}\quad  q :=\frac{R}{4\lambda \sqrt{k}}\left(\frac{2\delta^2}{81R^2}\right)^k.
equation

nodes.name: Theorem 2.5: aligned aligned
nodes.statement:
\caption{Construct a one-layer NN separating two finite sets with a margin}

algorithmic[1]
\Require Two $\delta$-separated finite sets $X^{+}, X^{-}\subset R\mathbb{B}_{2}^{d}$ and $\gamma \in [0, \max(\delta^2/8Rd, \delta^2/18R\sqrt{k})]$.
\Ensure A one-layer neural network $\Phi$ such that $\Phi(X^{+})$ and $\Phi(X^{-})$ are linearly separable.

\For{$i = 1,2,\ldots,N$}
\State $x_i \gets x$ where $x$ has the $i$-th largest norm in $X^+ \cup X^-$.
\EndFor
\For{$i = 1,2,\ldots,N$}

    \State Find $w\in \mathbb{S}^{d-1}$ and $b\in \mathbb{R}$ such that $w^{\intercal}x_i +b\geq \gamma$ and $w^{\intercal}x_j+b\leq -\gamma$ for all $j > i$ and $\sigma(x_i) \neq \sigma(x_j)$. If no such $j$ exists, ask $w^{\intercal}x_i +b\geq \gamma$ and $w^{\intercal}x +b \leq 0$ for some $x\in R\mathbb{B}_2^d$.
    
    \State $w_i \gets w$, $b_i \gets b$, $h_i \gets$ the function $w^{\intercal}_ix + b_i$ 

\EndFor
\State $W \gets$ the matrix with row vectors $w_i^{\intercal}$
\State $b \gets$ the vector with components $b_i$
\State \Return the function $\Phi(x)=\relax(Wx + b)$
algorithmic

For any two $\delta$-separated finite sets $X^{+}, X^{-}\subset R\mathbb{B}_{2}^{d}$, define $x_i$ and $\sigma$ as in alg:det_onelayer and (2.1). Consider the random affine function $h(z)=v^{\intercal}z+t$ where $t\in \mathbb{R},v\in \mathbb{R}^d$ are independent random variables with $t\sim\mathrm{Unif}\left([-\lambda, \lambda]\right)$ and the distribution of $v$ is specified below. For any $\gamma>0$, let
\[ B_{i}:=\left\lbrace h(x_{i})\geq \gamma \right\rbrace\cap \bigcap_{j:j>i, \sigma(x_i) \neq\sigma(x_j)  }\left\lbrace h(x_{j})\leq -\gamma \right\rbrace\]
for each $i\in [N]$. Recall $p$ from (1.1) and $q$ from (1.4). Then, there exists some $C=C(\delta, R)>0$ in the definition (1.3) of $k$ such that the following hold:
enumerate
    \item[(i)] For all $i$ and $\gamma \leq {\delta^{2}}/{8Rd}$, $\mathbb{P} (B_{i})\geq p$ if $v\sim\mathrm{Unif} \left(\mathbb{S}^{d-1}\right)$ and $\lambda\geq R$.
    \item[(ii)] For all $i$ and $\gamma \leq {\delta^{2}}/{8Rd}$, $\mathbb{P} (B_{i})\geq p/10$ if $v\sim \relax(0, I_{d})$ and $\lambda\geq 3R\sqrt{d}$.
    \item[(iii)] For all $i$ and $\gamma \leq {\delta^{2}}/{18R\sqrt{k}}$, $\mathbb{P} (B_{i})\geq q$ if $v\sim \relax(0, I_{d})$ and $\lambda\geq 9R\sqrt{k}/8$.
enumerate

nodes.name: Theorem 2.6: aligned aligned
nodes.statement:
\caption{Separate the image of the sets under the output of alg:det_onelayer}

algorithmic[1]
\Require Two $\delta$-separated finite sets $X^{+}, X^{-}\subset R\mathbb{B}_2^d$ and parameter $\gamma$ satisfying the input conditions of alg:det_onelayer, and the output $\Phi$ of alg:det_onelayer on $X^{+}, X^{-}$, and $\gamma$.
\Ensure A hyperplane $H\subset \mathbb{R}^N$ separating $\Phi(X^+)$ and $\Phi(X^-)$ with margin at least $\sqrt{N}\mathcal{M}(\gamma, N)$.
\For{$i = N,N-1,\ldots,1$}
    \State $a_i\gets\sigma(x_i)\left(1+\left\vert\sum_{j=i+1}^Na_j(\Phi(x_i))_j\right\vert\right)/\gamma$.
\EndFor
\State \Return the hyperplane $H(z)=a^{\intercal}z$ where $a=(a_i)_i\in\mathbb{R}^N$.
algorithmic

For output $\Phi$ of alg:det_onelayer on any sets $X^{+}, X^{-}$ and parameter $\gamma$ satisfying the input conditions, $\Phi (X^{+})$ and $\Phi (X^{-})$ are linearly separable with margin at least $\sqrt{N}\mathcal{M}(\gamma, N)$ in (1.1).

nodes.name: Theorem 3.1
nodes.statement:
Let $X^{+}, X^{-}\subset R\mathbb{B}_{2}^{d}$ be any two $\delta$-separated sets and $k$ as defined in (1.3). For any parameter $\gamma\in [0, \max(\delta^2/8Rd, \delta^2/18R\sqrt{k})]$, let $N$ be the $(\delta, 8R^2/\gamma )$-mutual complexity of $X^+$ and $X^-$. Let centers $C^{+}$ and $C^{-}$ be as guaranteed by 1.2. Recall $\mathcal{M}$ from (1.1). We have
enumerate
    \item[(i)] $C^+$ and $C^-$ with parameter $\gamma$ satisfy the input conditions of alg:det_onelayer.
    \item[(ii)] Let $\Phi$ be the output of alg:det_onelayer on $C^+$ and $C^-$ with parameter $\gamma$. Then, $\Phi(X^+)$ and $\Phi(X^-)$ are linearly separable with margin at least $\sqrt{N}\mathcal{M}(\gamma/2, N)$.
enumerate

nodes.name: Lemma 2.2
nodes.statement:
Fix $d \in \mathbb{Z}_{\geq 2}$. Denote the convex hull of $X$ by $\mathrm{conv}(X)$.
enumerate
\item For any $0\leq r\leq 2$, $u\in \mathbb{S}^{d-1}$, and $v\sim\mathrm{Unif} (\mathbb{S}^{d-1})$, we have \[\mathbb{P}_{v} \left(\Vert u-v\Vert \leq r\right)\geq \frac{1}{2}\left(\frac{r}{2}\right)^{d-1}.\]
\item For any set $X\subset \mathbb{R}^d$ and $c\in\mathrm{conv}(X)$, there exists $x\in X$ with $\Vert x\Vert\geq \Vert c\Vert$. Moreover, for any vector $g\in\mathbb{R}^d$, there exists some $x\in X$ with $g^{\intercal}x\geq g^{\intercal}c$.
enumerate

nodes.name: Lemma 2.3
nodes.statement:
Let $z\sim \chi_{d}^{2}$ be the chi-squared distributions with parameter $d$.
enumerate
\item For $v\sim \relax(0, I_{d})$, $\rho := \Vert v\Vert $ satisfies $\rho^2\sim \chi^2_{d}$, and $\widehat{v}:=v/\rho\sim \mathrm{Unif}(\mathbb{S}^{d-1})$. Moreover, $\rho$ and $\widehat{v}$ are independent.

\item$\mathbb{P}(z-d\geq 2\sqrt{dx}+2x)\leq e^{-x}$ and $\mathbb{P}(d-z\geq 2\sqrt{dx})\leq e^{-x}$ for all $x>0$.
enumerate
